mechanism_claims.claim_text: Molecular dynamics simulations provide computational context that selected AMPs can interact with bacterial inner-membrane models and human plasma-membrane models; this is not treated as direct killing evidence.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: reported de novo AMPs, especially potent Fig. 4 candidates
mechanism_claims.limitations: Computational membrane insertion/contact evidence supports mechanism plausibility only.
mechanism_claims.classification_basis: Fig. 3 and article text describe MD simulations of AMP interactions with model membranes; this is computational support only.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Resistance-passage experiments tracked daily MICs for six potent AMPs over 21 days and reported no resistance development relative to imipenem control.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Resistance outcome is a phenotype, not a molecular target assignment.
mechanism_claims.classification_basis: Fig. 5a tracks resistance/MIC phenotype over serial passage and does not establish a direct molecular target.
supporting_assay_types: 21-day serial passage daily MIC resistance assay

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Propidium iodide plate-reader and microscopy assays support membrane permeabilization context for E. coli cells treated with selected AMPs at 4x MIC.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: selected potent AMPs against E. coli MG1655

method_locator.locator: pdf:Methods:Mode of action assay and microscopy using propidium iodide

mechanism_claims.limitations: Supports membrane-permeability involvement; does not define a single molecular receptor or target.
mechanism_claims.classification_basis: Fig. 5c-d and Methods lines 1587-1607 provide direct PI uptake and microscopy evidence for membrane permeability context.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Outer membrane vesicle quantification at quarter-MIC was tested as an E. coli stress response/context assay; polymyxin B was the strongly different comparison group in the figure caption.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: selected potent AMPs against E. coli MG1655
mechanism_claims.limitations: This contextual assay is not promoted to direct AMP mechanism when the figure reports polymyxin B as the only significantly different group.
mechanism_claims.classification_basis: Fig. 5b reports OMV release/stress-response context; the six AMPs were not the significantly different group, so this is phenotype/context support, not direct mechanism closure.
